findings.title: Reconcile can declare a running mutation not applied
findings.why_it_matters: After a mutation times out or loses its reply, reconcile can return not_applied and arm a retry while the original mutation is still queued or executing; the first mutation can subsequently land. The engine continues handling the original connection after the adapter drops it, and its content reads do not take the mutation lock, so a point-in-time content comparison cannot establish the operation's final outcome. A durable operation identifier and an engine-side final-status/barrier check are needed before returning a definitive result. A lost-reply write that succeeded and was subsequently changed is reported not_applied, and the server re-arms a retry against the newer contents; the retry can overwrite another writer's update. Conversely, matching bytes can predate a failed or never-applied mutation, so applied is not proved either. A snapshot comparison cannot answer the promised historical outcome without a durable mutation identifier and journal or commit lookup.
